comments.text:
Yes, visually it looks quite beautiful. However, this geography actually creates significant challenges:

First of all, Turkey lies within the Alpine-Himalayan earthquake belt; furthermore, due to its rugged, folded terrain, there is very little flat land. While this geographical diversity fosters a wide variety of food products, it also results in a major lack of capacity. This situation has caused a persistent lack of economic depth in the region since ancient times, with the countries experiencing a crisis roughly every 20 to 25 years. Because it is situated within this mountainous belt, it is relatively poor in underground resources compared to other countries in the region. With a cold north and an extremely hot, arid south, the country’s economy is structured much like in many other nations with industry concentrated in the north, agriculture in the central regions, and tourism driving the economy in the south. It faces immense difficulties stemming from neighboring states regarding wars, crises, disasters, and migration.
